title: Optimal entanglement-assisted source coding under a balanced-difference promise
abstract: Entanglement can reduce the communication required for coding tasks, but establishing the minimum achievable cost is essential to understanding its limits. We address this question in a zero-error source-coding task where Alice receives a word and Bob knows an unordered pair of candidates containing it. Alice does not know the pair and must enable Bob to identify her word without error using shared entanglement and one classical message. The candidates satisfy a balanced-difference promise: for words in $\mathbb{Z}_q^n$ with $n=q\ell$, each residue modulo $q$ occurs exactly $\ell$ times in their coordinatewise difference. For all integers $q\geq2$ and $\ell\geq1$, we prove that the task requires exactly $n$ messages when $(q-1)\ell$ is even and two messages when it is odd. These minima allow arbitrary finite-dimensional shared states independent of the inputs and arbitrary local measurements. In even parity, this establishes optimality of an existing entanglement-assisted protocol. In odd parity, an explicit deterministic protocol achieves the optimum of one bit without entanglement. Our proof combines Fourier analysis with a combinatorial counting argument to determine the smallest eigenvalue of the associated graphs. In even parity, this resolves the spectral assertion of Cao et al.'s Conjecture 6.3 for balanced cyclic generalized Hadamard graphs. Together with an explicit odd-parity bipartition, this determines the quantum chromatic number as $n$ in even parity and $2$ in odd parity, where the classical chromatic number is also $2$. All lemmas, theorems, and corollaries are formalized and verified in Lean.
summary: This paper establishes the exact minimum number of classical messages needed for an entanglement-assisted source coding task under a specific 'balanced-difference promise.' It achieves this by mapping the problem to graph theory and using Fourier analysis to determine spectral properties. The results provide concrete bounds that separate classical communication limits from quantum communication limits.
main_problem: The paper determines the minimum communication cost (number of classical messages) required for a zero-error source-coding task when entanglement assistance is available.
main_result: The minimum message count is $n$ if $(q-1)\ell$ is even, and 2 if $(q-1)\ell$ is odd, establishing optimality for both cases.
method: The analysis combines Fourier analysis with combinatorial counting arguments, mapping the coding problem to graph spectral properties (eigenvalues) and graph coloring.
model_or_system: The model is a zero-error source-coding task involving a word $x$ and a pair of candidates $\{u, v\}$ satisfying a balanced-difference promise on $\mathbb{Z}_q^n$. This is analyzed using the associated graph $\Omega(\mathbb{Z}_q)^n$.
key_observables: Minimum number of classical messages required for zero-error decoding; the graph's least adjacency eigenvalue ($	au$).
important_parameters: Alphabet size $q$, word length $n$, and the parameter $\ell$ derived from the balanced-difference promise.
main_assumptions: The results hold for arbitrary finite-dimensional shared states and local measurements; the analysis relies on resolving spectral assertions related to graph theory conjectures.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the entanglement-assisted protocol setup and the $n$-message protocol, while other figures detail graph structures, spectral calculations, and the relationship between valid/invalid word assignments via swapping.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the coding problem and the balanced-difference promise, moving through graph theory and spectral analysis to establish lower bounds, and finally proving optimality for both even and odd parity cases.
why_interesting: The rigorous determination of quantum communication bounds using spectral graph theory provides deep insights into the fundamental limits of quantum information processing, connecting coding theory to algebraic graph theory.
